newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC sets new utility merger policy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC sets new utility merger policy.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday adopted new guidelines for approving electric utility mergers, focusing on the effects of a merger on competition, rates and regulation.
The commission adopted guidelines used by the Justice Department and Federal Trade Commission to review the impact of a merger on competition.
The commission said it would also focus on the impact that a merger would have on customer rates and would ask merger applicants to take steps to protect rate payers from sharp price increases.

The commission, which has been heavily critized for taking too long to review merger applications in a rapidly changing market, said it would aim to issue decisions within 12 to 15 months of receiving a completed merger application.
Commissioners, who approved the new guidelines unanimously, said the main goal of their policy statement was to make sure that new merged utilities did not thwart a competitive market.
"We do not want to see mergers that are counter to that goal," FERC Chairwoman Elizabeth Moler said.

Updating a 30-year-old policy for reviewing mergers, the commission said it would no longer try to measure the cost and benefits of a merger. Nine utility mergers worth about $25 billion are now pending before the commission.
